**Visual observations:**
- Soybean trifoliate leaves, lower canopy plant
- Numerous small to medium irregular brown/tan lesions scattered across all three leaflets
- Lower-right leaflet shows prominent yellow halos surrounding necrotic brown spots
- Upper-left leaflet shows smaller, scattered dark brown spots
- Some lesions appear to have coalesced into larger blotches
- No obvious angular (vein-limited) pattern
- No gray centers with red borders (not frogeye)
- No powdery or fuzzy growth visible

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Small, irregularly shaped dark brown lesions that coalesce; yellowing spreads beyond necrotic area; lower canopy — fits well.
- **Bacterial_Blight**: Angular/vein-limited lesions with yellowish-green halos; dead tissue falls out (ragged). The yellow halos are prominent here, but the lesions are not clearly angular.
- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: Gray centers with reddish-brown margins — not matching; these lesions are uniformly tan/brown without gray centers.
- **Downy_mildew**: Pale yellow spots on upper surface with gray tufts below — lesions here are clearly brown/necrotic, not pale yellow.

The scattered distribution, irregular brown spots coalescing, and yellowing beyond necrosis with no clear angular/vein-limited pattern best matches **Septoria_brown_spot**. The yellow areas could reflect the "leaf yellowing expands far beyond the necrotic region" characteristic. Lower canopy location also aligns.
